newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro stocks at highs despite data caution.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro stocks at highs despite data caution.

text.p: London and Paris shares nudged their way to trading records on Tuesday but most European financial markets were cautious ahead of important U.S. economic data.
Bourses took their lead from another record close on Wall Street and calmer Asian markets but the main focus was on the U.S. inflation data for December.
U.S. bonds fell overnight as investors braced for a new round of data, which spilled over into Europe, where German and British government bonds both fell in early trade.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar steadied off its highs as traders awaited the U.S. consumer price inflation (CPI) and retail sales figures due at 1330 GMT.

"The dollar trend is still fairly strong and we're looking for reasonably strong retail sales and CPI," said Tom Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull in London. "It should keep the dollar fairly well supported in anticipation of a Fed rate rise."
Analyst forecasts point to a December headline CPI rise of 0.3 percent with the core rate up 0.2 percent. Retail sales are expected to show a 0.5 percent increase.
After Monday's string of record closes among European bourses, several markets paused for breath.
But London and Paris remained buoyant around Monday's record levels and both the Stockholm and Helsinki bourses set new highs, too. Frankfurt, in contrast, slipped a little.
In London, the FTSE 100 index hit record highs above 4,127 points after rising nearly half a percent in early trade.

The rise defied some market expectations of consolidation but other traders argued the FTSE could rally further with investment funds flush with cash and the Dow's bull run showing no sign of stumbling.
"It would probably not take too much to push the market higher from these levels," said one dealer.

Monday's weak British producer price data eased concerns that Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George would agree an interest rate rise at a policy meeting on Wednesday.
Airport operator BAA was up 13-1/2p at 498-1/2 after posting a 5.5 percent rise in passenger numbers in 1996, while BT rose 6p to 411-1/2 after announcing cuts in the price of international calls.
In Paris the blue chip CAC-40 index surpassed Monday's intraday record by a fraction of a point, hitting 2,371.94 before easing.
Although traders said prices needed to consolidate before attacking the next big psychological level of 2,400, the market remained buoyant.

By 1030 GMT the index was up 8.38 at 2,369.65 points, with Rhone-Poulenc rising sharply on market talk of a possible alliance or merger in the pharmaceuticals sector. Its stock surged 4.92 percent to stand at 174.8 francs.
German shares started bourse trade slightly lower, rangebound ahead of the U.S. data.
Pharmaceuticals company Hoechst weakened 37 pfennigs after the U.S. Food and Drugs Authority proposed withdrawing approval for its Seldane allergy drug.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was trading at 116.42 yen and 1.5894 marks compared with 116.30 and 1.5890 late in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index was up 19.1 points, or 0.47 percent, at 4,126.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 8.38 points, or 0.35 percent, at 2,369.65.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 1.29 points, or 0.04 percent, at 2,953.27.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed at $357.30 against $359.60 previously, with the bullion market confused and nervous after news that the Dutch central bank had sold some of its gold reserves. Silver was indicated two cents lower at $4.70.
